section.title: The ooSQLCollation Class
section.para: An ooSQLCollation object represents a collation of an ooSQLite package: a comparison function, written in C or C++, that a package describes in its collation table. The C code stays in the shared library of the package; the object holds what ooSQLite needs to register it: its name and its entry points. Programs do not create ooSQLCollation objects: ooSQLite creates them.

The object is obtained with the getCollation method of an ooSQLPackage object, and its only use is as the argument of the createCollation method of the ooSQLiteConnection class, which registers the collation on the connection under the name given there. The same object can be registered on any number of connections, and under different names. register registers all the collations of a package at once, and autoCollation makes one automatic.

section.title: new (Class method)
section.para: Creates an ooSQLCollation object. ooSQLite uses it internally; programs obtain the object with the getCollation method of an ooSQLPackage object.

listitem.para:
The only argument is:
entry [required]
A Buffer object with a copy of the description that the package gives in C. Only ooSQLite can create it.
A Rexx program can not create the Buffer object that new needs, so new invoked from a program raises a syntax error: 88.901 without an argument, and 88.900 with any other argument.

&changed11;A subclass of ooSQLCollation whose init method does not forward to the init method of ooSQLCollation creates objects that are not initialized. createCollation raises an execution error, 98.900, when it is given one. Before ooSQLite 1.1 it crashed the interpreter.

This example registers the ebcdic collation of the examplePackage package, which sorts as EBCDIC does: lowercase letters, then uppercase letters, then digits:
.ooSQLExtensions~loadPackage('examplepackage') package = .ooSQLExtensions~getPackage('examplePackage') collation = package~getCollation('ebcdic') say collation say db~createCollation('ebcdic', collation) sql = "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES ('1'), ('A'), ('a'))" - "SELECT group_concat(x, ' ') AS v FROM (SELECT x FROM t ORDER BY x COLLATE ebcdic);" say db~exec(sql, .true)[1]['V'] /* Output: an ooSQLCollation 0 a A 1 */

Invoking new from a program raises a syntax error:
signal on syntax collation = .ooSQLCollation~new say 'not reached' syntax: say condition('O')~code condition('O')~message /* Output: 88.901 Missing argument; argument 1 is required. */
